about.title: Larkspur Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Larkspur is a small city, but its households buy the same appliances, vehicle parts, tools, and consumer goods sold everywhere else in Marin County — and sometimes those products fail. California generally treats these cases under strict liability, meaning an injured person doesn't have to prove a manufacturer was careless, only that the product itself was defective in design, manufacturing, or warning, and that the defect caused harm. That standard matters in a town like Larkspur, where a single faulty part in a car navigating US-101 or Sir Francis Drake Boulevard, or a malfunctioning household item, can lead to real injury with real medical bills. If a product hurt you here, holding onto it exactly as it is — don't repair it, discard it, or alter it — can matter a great deal to a claim. LawProactive doesn't practice law; we simply connect you, at no cost, with an independent attorney who can look at what happened and explain your options.

whyChoose.title: Why Strict Liability Matters for Larkspur Residents

items.title: You Don't Have to Prove Carelessness
items.desc: Under California's strict liability rule, a manufacturer's intent or care level isn't the focus — what matters is whether the product itself was defective and caused your injury.

items.title: Multiple Parties Can Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and even the retailer who sold the item in Larkspur can potentially be held liable, which widens the paths toward accountability.

items.title: The Product Itself Is Key Evidence
items.desc: Because these claims often hinge on showing a design, manufacturing, or warning defect, preserving the item exactly as it was at the time of injury can strengthen a case significantly.

items.question: Do I need to prove the manufacturer was negligent?
items.answer: No — California generally applies strict liability to defective product claims, so the focus is on the product's condition and whether it caused your injury, not on proving carelessness. An independent attorney can walk you through what evidence typically supports this kind of claim.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Keep it in its current condition and avoid repairing, cleaning, or throwing it away, since the item itself is often central evidence in a product liability case. Store it somewhere safe and, if possible, keep the packaging or manuals too.

items.question: Is this only about products bought in stores in Larkspur?
items.answer: Not necessarily — defective product claims can involve anything from vehicle parts used on corridors like US-101 or Sir Francis Drake Boulevard to household goods bought anywhere. What matters is where the defect originated, not just where or when it was purchased.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything to connect me with an attorney?
items.answer: No, LawProactive is a free service and we are not a law firm ourselves. Attorneys in our network typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation.
